passages.text:
And I set out my purpose from the beginning, how I had exhausted myself in insoluble inquiries, and everything that I disclosed to you at the outset, so that I may not write the same things again. I said, “I am quite ready to travel with you—for, though I do not know how, this is what I gladly desire. But first I want to be fully assured about the truth, so that I may know whether the soul proves to be mortal or is immortal; whether, if it is eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here; whether there is ever anything just or pleasing to God; whether the world came into being and why it came into being; whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved; and whether it will be better or will not even exist.” And, to avoid speaking item by item, I said that I wanted to learn these things and those that follow from them.

In reply he said, “I will briefly give you knowledge of the things that exist, Clement; for the present, hear from that knowledge.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: I had exhausted myself in insoluble inquiries
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive form of κενόω is figurative here: the inquiries had left the speaker spent or emptied, while ἄπορος describes questions offering no way through.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦτο γὰρ οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως χαίρων θέλω
lexical_decisions.chosen: for, though I do not know how, this is what I gladly desire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the parenthetical uncertainty of οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως and the positive force of χαίρων θέλω; alternatively, the phrase may mean “for somehow—I do not know how—I gladly desire this.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: first I want to be fully assured about the truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: πληροφορέω denotes being brought to full assurance or certainty, not merely receiving information.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ εἰ ἀίδιος οὖσα περὶ ὧν ἔπραξεν ἐνταῦθα ἔχει κριθῆναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: whether, if it is eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering takes ἀίδιος οὖσα conditionally because the preceding question leaves the soul’s immortality unsettled. The participle can alternatively state the circumstance or premise: “whether, being eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here.” This is an interpretive ambiguity rather than source corruption.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: περὶ ὧν ἔπραξεν ἐνταῦθα ἔχει κριθῆναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: it is to be judged for what it has done here
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἔχει with the infinitive expresses what is appointed or bound to occur; the feminine subject remains the soul.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἴ τι ποτ᾿ ἔστιν δίκαιον ἢ ἀρέσκον θεῷ
lexical_decisions.chosen: whether there is ever anything just or pleasing to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: τι ποτε asks whether any such thing exists at all, while both adjectives remain coordinated.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ εἰ κρείττων ἔσται ἢ οὐδὲ ἔσται
lexical_decisions.chosen: and whether it will be better or will not even exist
lexical_decisions.rationale: οὐδέ supplies emphatic negation: the alternative to the world being better is that it will not even exist, not merely that it will no longer exist.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾿ εἶδος λέγω
lexical_decisions.chosen: to avoid speaking item by item
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατ᾿ εἶδος can mean by individual form, category, or particular item; the context abbreviates a longer enumeration.

lexical_decisions.chosen: for the present, hear from that knowledge
lexical_decisions.rationale: τὰ νῦν is temporal, while αὐτῆς most naturally refers back to the promised knowledge; “hear the present points from it” is also possible.
